## What each form conserves (summary and oracle guide) {#sec-ch06-conserves}

### Summary

Two facts set the default case. The default of `gravity-work` is `face`, and with it the corrected-PE face work of
@sec-ch06-dwork, so a deck that omits the key conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$, not $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$. And the corrected-PE work
runs on `gnomonic-equiangle` (cubed-sphere) grids as well as Cartesian and spherical-polar ones; there it books one
more term, for the offset between the cell's volume centroid and `x1v`.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Says, for each gravity-work form, which invariant is exact, per stage or per step, and which test is its oracle.

**Data.** The integrated invariants $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ and $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ [J]; the logged `ie=`, `pe=` and `fixgrav=`.

**Placement.** A guide across @sec-ch06-cell to @sec-ch06-vic; it adds no step of its own.

**Activation.** `gravity-work`, default `face`, with `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` on by default; the fixer only with `cell`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact means to round-off on a closed column; open $x_1$ boundaries change every invariant.

**Evidence.** The oracle of each form in @tbl-ch06-conserves-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal E=E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ [J] as a function of the state;
$x_{1v,i}$ [m] the stored cell centre `x1v`; $o_i=x_{1,i}-x_{1v,i}$ [m] the offset of the volume centroid from it, as
in @sec-ch06-dwork. $x_{1,i}$, $x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}$[^rg-fbecacf7f134] and $\delta_i=x_{1,i}-x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}$ are the centroid, face
midpoint and centroid offset defined in @sec-appa.

Every form in this chapter is the identity @eq-ch06-dwork-booked with a different discrete potential energy, so
the question "what does it conserve" is "which $P$ does it use, and where does it stop using it". The face form
uses $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$ everywhere; the corrected-PE work uses the fourth-order $P$ of @eq-ch06-dwork-pe; the cell
form uses none and leaves the defect @eq-ch06-cell-defect, which the fixer removes once per step; `face-wallc`
uses $\mathrm{PE}_d$ except in its two $x_1$ wall cells. The logged `ie=` (the integrated total energy $E_{\mathrm{tot}}$) plus `pe=` is the
invariant of the run's own form, because `pe=` logs $P$ whenever the corrected-PE work is active and
$\mathrm{PE}_d$ otherwise. An oracle that checks $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ on a default run therefore measures the wrong
quantity.

### Derivation

The template @eq-ch06-dwork-booked conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ exactly on a closed column for any $P$; the forms differ only
in $P$, and the derivations are in the sections that own them. The face form is $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$
(@eq-ch06-dwork-face). The corrected-PE work is @eq-ch06-dwork-d, conserving @eq-ch06-dwork-pe; its stage-by-stage argument extends to the step in three steps (@sec-ch06-dwork):

1. $\mathcal E=E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ is linear in the state, and $\mathcal E(\Delta t\,\mathcal L)=0$ on a closed column by
   @eq-ch06-dwork-booked.
2. A stage gives $\mathcal E(\mathbf U^{\mathrm{new}})=w_0^{(s)}\mathcal E(\mathbf U^n)+w_1^{(s)}\mathcal E(\mathbf U)$, and
   $w_0^{(s)}+w_1^{(s)}=1$ for every stage of the four integrators at the pyharp pin, `rk1`, `rk2`, `rk3` and `rk3s4`
   ([`pyharp integrator.cpp:33-81`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L33-L81)).
3. By induction over the stages, $\mathcal E(\mathbf U)=\mathcal E(\mathbf U^n)$ after each stage, hence after the step.

It is the unit sum $w_0+w_1=1$ that the argument uses, not convexity: non-negative weights are not needed.

In the implicit solve the matrix part @eq-ch06-dwork-couple plus the remainder
@eq-ch06-dwork-remainder book the work of the mass actually moved. The cell form leaves @eq-ch06-cell-defect per
stage; the fixer @eq-ch06-fixer-fix subtracts the stage-weighted sum after the last stage, so $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$
closes per step but not per stage. `face-wallc` books $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$ instead of $W^{\mathrm{face}}$ in the
two $x_1$ wall cells, so its $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ defect is their cell-minus-face work (@sec-ch06-face).

On a `gnomonic-equiangle` grid the corrected-PE work books one more term, derived in @sec-ch06-dwork as
@eq-ch06-dwork-cs: the stored cell centre `x1v`, $x_{1v,i}$, is the face midpoint $x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}$ there, not the
volume centroid $x_{1,i}$, and with the code offset $o_i=x_{1,i}-x_{1v,i}$ the work gains $g_1o_i\dot\rho_i$. In four steps:

1. The corrected $P$ is expanded about the centroid, so its potential is $\phi(x_{1,i})$.
2. $\phi$ is linear, so $\phi(x_{1,i})=\phi(x_{1v,i})-g_1o_i$ exactly.
3. The code writes $\phi$ at `x1v`, so $P_i$ gains $-g_1V_io_i\rho_i$, and @eq-ch06-dwork-booked turns that into
   the extra work $g_1o_i\dot\rho_i$.
4. On Cartesian and spherical-polar grids `x1v` is the centroid, $o_i=0$, and the term vanishes. On the
   `gnomonic-equiangle` grid $x_{1v,i}=x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}$, so there $o_i$ equals appendix A's $\delta_i$.

The term is booked by `corrected_pe_work` under `radial_mid`
({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp corrected_pe_work >}}), in the logged $P$ and the post-solve remainder,
and on the diagonal of the implicit energy row as `rx_mid`
({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}). Its checks are those of
@sec-ch06-dwork (`[CS1]`, `[CS2]`); `[C25]` of `derivation_check.py` is step 2.[^ch06-cons-chk]

### Numerical method

@tbl-ch06-conserves-summary is the oracle guide. "Stage" means $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ is exact after every RK stage, "step" only
after the whole step. Exact means to round-off on a closed column (reflecting $x_1$ walls); with an open $x_1$
boundary every invariant changes by the potential-energy flux through it, and the fixer refuses that case.

| form | exact invariant | when | logged | oracle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cell`, no fixer | none | | `ie=`+`pe=` drifts | `test_gravity_work_fixer_python` |
| `cell` + fixer | $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ | step, explicit and VIC | `ie=`+`pe=`, `fixgrav=` | `test_gravity_work_fixer_python` |
| `face`, switch 0 | $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ | stage, explicit and VIC | `ie=`+`pe=` | `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` |
| `face-wallc` | none in the wall cells | | `ie=`+`pe=` | reported only |
| `face` (default) | $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ | stage, explicit and VIC | `ie=`+`pe=` ($P$) | `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` |

: What each form conserves on a closed column, which logged sum measures it and which test checks it. "Switch 0"
is `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0`; the default `face` row also holds for grids with no corrected-PE form, as
`face` with switch 0. Tolerances and code links are in the Code and Tests layers. {#tbl-ch06-conserves-summary}

Where each form books its energy: the face form, the corrected-PE term and the cell work are all formed in step
(6) of `HydroImpl::forward`, once per stage, as `gravity_energy_correction`, and added to the energy row before
the implicit solve with `face` and an implicit scheme, after it otherwise (@sec-ch06-dwork). The fixer acts after
the last stage, once per step, so only the step closes under it. With an implicit scheme the VIC carries the
face form and the tridiagonal part of the corrected-PE term in its energy row, and the post-solve remainder books
the rest; under `face-wallc` the face work is swapped in after the solve (@sec-ch06-vic).

Block seams. At an internal $x_1$ seam the explicit corrected-PE work exchanges one row of the stage's density
change with the $x_1$ neighbour and takes the centred slope a single block would take; at a physical wall the
slope stays one-sided. The logged $P$ does the same with the exchanged ghost density. So a column split in $x_1$
conserves the one-block $P$, and the split state equals the unsplit one. The implicit scheme refuses any $x_1$
split, so the VIC row and its remainder never meet a seam. A periodic $x_1$ column keeps the one-sided slope at
its block edges, because $-g_1x_1$ jumps at the periodic face and has no single-valued $P$; setup warns once. No
new figure: the stencils are those of @fig-ch06-dwork-stencil, whose panel (c) shows the one-sided slope a periodic
column keeps at its block edges.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| default `face`; fixer default with `cell` | {{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `gravity_work` | `gravity-work` |
| fixer off for face forms | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `gravity_work_fixer` | `gravity-work-fixer` |
| grids with a corrected-PE form | {{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp x1_measure >}} | `x1_measure` | |
| where the corrected-PE work acts | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}} | `radial_exact_work` | `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` |
| corrected-PE work, seams | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `corrected_pe_work_seam` | `face` |
| cell work and fixer defect | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `gwfix_stage` | `cell` |
| face minus cell, wall cells | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `gravity_energy_correction` | `face-wallc` |
| stage weight of the defect | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `cw` | `cell` |
| fixer heat, counted | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_gravity_work_fixer >}} | `add_gravity_work_fix` | `cell` |
| $\mathrm{PE}_d$ or $P$ summed | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}} | `pe_sum` | |
| `pe=` printed | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}} | `pe_sum` | |
| `fixgrav=` printed | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}} | `gravity_work_fix` | `gravity-work-fixer` |
| `ie=` label | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::print_cycle_info >}} | `print_cycle_diagnostics` | |
| implicit needs one $x_1$ block | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}} | `TORCH_CHECK` | `implicit-scheme` |

: Code map of where each form books its gravity work and where the logged sums are formed. {#tbl-ch06-conserves-code}

1. `from_yaml` sets `gravity_work` to `face` when the key is absent and `gravity_work_fixer` to true only for
   `cell` ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}});
   the `HydroImpl` constructor forces `gravity_work_fixer` off for a face form
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
2. `radial_exact_work` is true for `face`, $g_1\neq0$, the switch on, and a grid whose `x1_measure` is not
   `none`: Cartesian, spherical-polar or gnomonic-equiangle
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}).
   On another grid setup warns once in the `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` under `x1_measure`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}),
   and with a periodic $x_1$ in the `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` under `periodic_x1`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
3. Each stage, the corrected-PE term is added to the face work, by `corrected_pe_work` on a block with no $x_1$
   neighbour and by `corrected_pe_work_seam` with the neighbour's density change at a seam
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
4. With `cell`, `gwfix_stage` collects the stage defect for the fixer
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}),
   weighted by `cw` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}});
   otherwise `gravity_energy_correction` replaces the cell work, kept in the wall cells under `face-wallc`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
5. After the last stage the fixer adds `efix` per unit mass and counts $-\mathcal D$ with `add_gravity_work_fix`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_gravity_work_fixer >}}),
   committed when the step is accepted.
6. The cycle diagnostics sum `pe` as $\rho\phi$ at `x1v`, minus `corrected_pe_work_seam` of the density when
   `radial_exact_work` holds, into `pe_sum`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}),
   print it as `pe=` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}),
   and print the fixer's run-to-date energy correction `gravity_work_fix` as `fixgrav=` only when the fixer is on
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}).

So `pe=` is $P$ (with $\phi$ at the volume centroid on the cubed sphere) under the corrected-PE work and
$\mathrm{PE}_d$ under every other form. `fixgrav=` is the total energy the fixer has added over the run's
accepted steps, in J, not reduced per step and not carried across a restart; under `cell` + fixer, `ie=`+`pe=`
is constant and `fixgrav=` records how much heat that took.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` | per-step $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$, explicit and VIC, incl. `cs`, `cs_vic` | $10^{-14}$ rel. | `EP_TOL` |
| `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` | logged `ie=`+`pe=` equals $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ (on), $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ (off) | $10^{-11}$ | `DIAG_TOL` |
| `test_gravity_work_fixer_python` | `cell` + fixer keeps $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$; no fixer drifts | $10^{-12}$; $>100\times$ | `TOL` |
| `test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact` | 2 vs 1 $x_1$ blocks: gap 0, split $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ drift | exact; $10^{-13}$ | the centred seam slope |
| `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` | $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ (switch 0) or $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ under VIC | $10^{-11}$ rel. | `EPE_TOL` |

: Oracles of each form; assertions read from the test sources at the pin, not run here.
{#tbl-ch06-conserves-tests}

The corrected-PE oracle sets `EP_TOL` and `DIAG_TOL` among the module constants of
{{< code tests/test_gravity_work_radial_exact.py >}}
and runs its cubed-sphere cases `cs` and `cs_vic`, one gnomonic-equiangle block with radial flow only, defined at
{{< code tests/test_gravity_work_radial_exact.py CASES >}}.
The fixer oracle compares the drift with `TOL` in both directions at
{{< code tests/test_gravity_work_fixer.py main >}};
its `cell` arms state `cell` explicitly, because the default is `face`. The seam test requires a gap of exactly 0 with the
switch on and at most $10^{-13}$ with it off, in `radial_exact_split_gap`
({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp radial_exact_split_gap >}}).
`face-wallc` has no conservation oracle; `test_gravity_work_fixer` only reports its drift.

Evidence:

- Cubed sphere, six panels, flow across the panel seams, both $x_1$ walls closed, $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ from the logged energy
  and `pe=`: per step $1.88\times10^{-15}$ explicit and $3.14\times10^{-15}$ VIC; with the centroid term left out
  of $P$, $1.28\times10^{-10}$ and $2.57\times10^{-10}$.[^ch06-cons-cs]
- $x_1$ seams, explicit: `radial_exact_split_gap` at $n_1$ = 32, 64, 128 is 0, and `test_pref_local_seam`, 4 blocks
  against 1, gives a relative density difference of $7\times10^{-15}$; with one-sided slopes at the seams (which the
  code takes only on a periodic column) the gap was $8.0\times10^{-7}$, $6.3\times10^{-8}$, $2.3\times10^{-9}$ and
  the density difference $2.7\times10^{-6}$.[^ch06-cons-seam]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
On a default run (`face`, switch on) every $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ check, including `gravity_work_defect()`, measures
the wrong invariant: check `ie=`+`pe=`. `fixgrav=` is printed only with `cell` + fixer.
:::

- `cell` without the fixer and `face-wallc` have no exact invariant $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$; neither has an oracle that bounds the
  drift.
- Periodic $x_1$: the corrected-PE work keeps the one-sided slope at block edges and $P$ is not defined; setup
  warns once. The fixer refuses periodic and open $x_1$.
- An implicit scheme refuses any $x_1$ split, so implicit runs have no seam case to test.
- VIC wall cells of the corrected-PE work are about second order, not fourth: the implicit correction flux is
  first-order upwind and $O(\Delta t)$;[^ch06-cons-302] conservation is unaffected.
- A lone gnomonic block with reflecting lateral walls loses mass under lateral flow, switch on or
  off;[^ch06-cons-301] the single-block ctest uses radial flow only.
- Grids other than Cartesian, spherical-polar and gnomonic-equiangle keep the plain face form and $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$.
- Untested combinations: @sec-ch12-matrix.

[^ch06-cons-302]: Recorded in chengcli/snapy#302.
